heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: Identify the schema namespace. Ignore the metadata declarations `_module`, `_interface`, and `_implements` for schema-declaration construction. The primary schema namespace is the longest common dot-segment prefix shared by all local qualified declarations that are not metadata declarations and not common-schema declarations. It MUST contain at least one segment and MUST be a proper prefix of every local declaration name. If `_interface` is present, its value MUST match the primary schema namespace. Exactly one primary schema namespace MUST be present in this revision. Every local declaration MUST use that namespace. A local non-metadata declaration without a qualified name in the primary namespace is invalid.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: Emit one `schema-declaration` for each local named type, method, method request, method response, and event. Method declaration bodies use `method-declaration`. For each method, set the request and response sensitivity fields from `_sensitive` as defined in Section 9.1. Type, request, response, and event declaration bodies use `schema-node`. The `schema-node` body of every method request, method response, and event declaration MUST be either a `map-schema` or a `choice-schema`. Every arm of such a `choice-schema` MUST be a `map-schema`. All emitted declarations MUST have distinct qualified names. A synthesized method name that collides with another declaration makes the contract invalid.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: For a concrete module schema, use an empty implemented-interface-root collection when `_implements` is absent. Otherwise, read one root from each direct byte-string literal element of its nonempty fixed-content array, in array order. The `_implements` rule MUST satisfy the syntax and ordering requirements in LOGOS-MODULE-INTERFACE Section 1.2. Each root MUST resolve to exactly one explicitly supplied interface document whose recomputed root matches that entry. Exact duplicate roots and two roots whose interface documents declare the same namespace are invalid. Interface and supporting schemas have no implemented-interface roots.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: Boolean and text-string literals translate to `literal-schema` with the corresponding `scalar-kind`. A non-negative integer literal translates with scalar kind `uint64` and MUST fit that type. A negative integer literal translates with scalar kind `int64` and MUST fit that type. A byte-string literal in `_implements` is role metadata and is handled before declaration construction. A byte-string literal in a schema declaration body is invalid.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: Local named references MUST preserve the referenced qualified name.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: They MUST NOT be replaced by the referenced declaration body when constructing the referring `schema-node`.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: The resulting plan MUST prove that no decoded value can match more than one arm.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: Source declaration order MUST NOT participate in plan construction or arm selection.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: The outcomes of every structural test, including its not-applicable outcome when defined, MUST assign every decoded value to exactly one outcome.

heading: 3.1 Logos Schema-Model Construction
text: An arm MUST remain a candidate unless its schema proves that it rejects the observed major type, scalar literal, tuple length, field value, or field presence.

text: Implementations MUST memoize reference results and detect recursive and mutually recursive reference components.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: Implementations MUST encode the identifier as UTF-8 text in canonical schema objects and MUST compare identifiers byte-for-byte.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: Unknown identifiers MUST be rejected unless the verifier explicitly supports the identifier or has an applicable compatibility profile.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: A future update to `cdCDDLe` that changes the Logos canonical schema model or the canonical schema bytes consumed by Logos MUST either define a new Logos semantic commitment-model revision identifier or define an explicit compatibility profile.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: A future semantic commitment-model revision must define whether it can verify old schema roots directly, translate old schema models into a newer model, or keep old roots in their original domain.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: The hash input for each hashed schema object MUST commit to both the object-kind domain tag and the semantic commitment-model revision identifier before committing to the Logos canonical object payload.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: A hash computed for one object kind MUST NOT be accepted as a hash for another object kind, even if the normalized payloads are otherwise identical.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: Schema references MAY identify schemas or schema subtrees defined under a different semantic commitment-model revision identifier.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: A verifier MUST NOT accept such a reference merely because the referenced hash matches.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: The verifier MUST either support the referenced semantic commitment-model revision directly or support an explicit compatibility profile that defines how objects from the referenced revision are verified in relation to objects from the referring revision.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: It must name the semantic commitment-model revisions it connects and the exact verification or translation rule it permits.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: If no applicable compatibility profile is available, the verifier MUST keep the referenced object in its original semantic domain and MUST NOT treat it as an object in the referring schema's semantic domain.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: Compatibility profiles MUST NOT weaken verifier policy.

heading: 6. Commitment Model Revision Identifier
text: A verifier or trust profile that requires a specific semantic commitment-model revision identifier, or a specific set of allowed identifiers, for a schema, package, method, value proof, or remote-runtime evidence MUST reject a different identifier unless the policy explicitly allows that identifier or an explicit compatibility profile for that identifier.
